content:
The test image shows a split soybean stem with grayish-white internal discoloration and dark streaking/browning along the pith and vascular tissue. This is a stem cross-section, not a leaf disease.

Key features:
- Split stem showing internal tissue
- Grayish-white to bleached pith
- Dark brown streaks along vascular bundles
- Dry, fibrous internal tissue
- No external white mycelium

This pattern strongly matches **Brown Stem Rot** (internal brown discoloration of the pith/vascular tissue when stem is split) or **Sudden Death Syndrome** (also shows internal discoloration). Let me view a Brown Stem Rot reference.

The Brown Stem Rot reference shows a split stem with dark brown/reddish-brown internal pith discoloration — very characteristic internal browning pattern.

Comparing to the test image: the test image shows a more mature/dry stem (harvested stage) with grayish-white pith and dark streaks. The reference Brown Stem Rot shows darker, more intensely brown pith in a green plant. However, at late season/harvest stage, Brown Stem Rot stems become dry with gray-white pith and brown vascular streaking — which matches the test image well.

The split stem presentation, the grayish-white bleached pith with dark brown vascular streaking running longitudinally, is classic Brown Stem Rot symptomology on mature/dry soybean stems.
